title: CONFIRMED at high: the HTTP server is built with zero inbound timeouts, so the 90s cfg.ReadTimeout is provably dead config — unauthenticated slowloris and never-expiring keep-alives are unmitigated, and the header-phase stall is structurally invisible to the only concurrency control (MaxConnections)
category: unauthenticated-denial-of-service / connection-exhaustion (slow-loris, idle keep-alive accumulation, slow-reader handler pinning)
evidence: Verified verbatim, no line drift. backend/cmd/server/main.go:126 is literally `srv := &http.Server{Addr: fmt.Sprintf(":%d", cfg.ListenPort), Handler: engine}` — no ReadHeaderTimeout, ReadTimeout, IdleTimeout, WriteTimeout or MaxHeaderBytes; grep `http\.Server` over backend/ returns this single hit (plus `err := srv.ListenAndServe()` at main.go:134), so there is no second listener and no wrapper that could impose a deadline. backend/internal/config/config.go:25-26 declares `ReadTimeout time.Duration` / `WriteTimeout time.Duration` and config.go:72-73 assigns `ReadTimeout: 90 * time.Second,` / `WriteTimeout: 0, // SSE 长连接不设总写超时，由逐请求 context 控制`; my independent grep for `cfg\.ReadTimeout|cfg\.WriteTimeout|\.ReadTimeout|\.WriteTimeout` across backend/**/*.go returns 'No matches found' — every other ReadTimeout/WriteTimeout identifier in the tree is a go-redis client option (quota/redis_limiter.go:47-48, slb/slb.go:79-80, admin/redis_mfa.go:73) or a test file (admin/auditws_test.go:126,160 SetReadDeadline). No non-test file contains SetReadDeadline/SetWriteDeadline/SetDeadline, http.TimeoutHandler or MaxHeaderBytes, and `net\.Listen` has 0 hits (no custom listener). The in-code rationale even cites the unwired property: gateway.go:494 `这与 WriteTimeout=0（"SSE 长连接不设总写超时"）的设计一致`. Downstream facts confirmed: gateway.go:322 `body, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(c.Request.Body, 16<<20))` and gateway.go:98 (same call for count_tokens) have no deadline; gateway.go:195 `if int64(snap.General.MaxConnections) > 0 && s.mx.Conns() >= int64(snap.General.MaxConnections) {` sits in AuthMiddleware, which Go only dispatches after the request headers are fully parsed, while the counter itself moves at gateway.go:300 `s.mx.ConnInc()` / :301 `defer s.mx.ConnDec()`; metrics.go:114-122 shows `conns` is a handler-scope gauge, so header-phase sockets contribute to nothing. Streams: gateway.go:496-505 applies DefaultTimeoutSeconds only under `if !cr.Stream {`, and the relay write is `func (s *SSEWriter) raw(line string) error { _, err := io.WriteString(s.w, line); if err == nil { s.flush() }; return err }` at sse.go:234-240 — no deadline, no ctx check, and the scan loop at gateway.go:654-718 never re-checks time.
impact: Availability of the whole product (single process serves gateway + admin + SPA), from an unauthenticated network position, with near-zero attacker cost. (a) Slowloris / idle accumulation: with ReadHeaderTimeout, ReadTimeout and IdleTimeout all effectively 0, Go applies no header deadline and no idle deadline (IdleTimeout falls back to ReadTimeout, which is unset), so a client dribbling header bytes holds a connection goroutine + readLoop goroutine + bufio.Reader + fd indefinitely and keep-alive sockets are never reaped. Because the stall happens before dispatch, gin.Recovery (main.go:95), the access-log closure (main.go:106-118, which logs only after c.Next()), AuthMiddleware and the MaxConnections guard are all bypassed — the pile-up is uncounted, unthrottled and invisible in the logs, and its only ceiling is the OS descriptor limit. Once that limit is reached Accept stops succeeding, so even GET /healthz (routes.go:18) stops answering, the compose healthcheck (docker-compose.yml:29) fails and `restart: unless-stopped` recycles the process into the same flood. (b) Slow-reader / slow-body pinning: with no server WriteTimeout and no per-write deadline, one client that stops reading blocks sse.go's io.WriteString forever and its ConnInc slot is never released (ConnDec is a handler-return defer), so a handful of sockets can hold Conns at General.MaxConnections (default 1000, settings/settings.go:32) and pin the entire data plane into 503 'gateway is overloaded' for every other key. The 'non-stream bounded' design fact holds only for the upstream leg (gateway.go:497-505), never for reading from or writing to the client.
corrections_to_filed_finding: Impact (b) is NOT 'fully unauthenticated' as filed on the cited line: /v1/* is registered as `gw := r.Group("/v1"); gw.Use(gws.AuthMiddleware())` (routes.go:27-28), so gateway.go:322 / :98 are only reached after a valid enabled sk- key and an IP allowlist pass (gateway.go:215-227). The unauthenticated body-read variant exists but on a different route — see verify-dos-4-2.

'a connection stalled in header/body reading is invisible to MaxConnections' is correct for the header phase and incorrect for the body phase: ConnInc (gateway.go:300) precedes the body read (:322), so body-phase stalls ARE counted and the guard (default 1000) sheds new traffic at that point. The consequence is '1000 permanently pinned handlers → service-wide 503', not unbounded handler growth.

'each request pins ... a 16 MiB ReadAll buffer' overstates per-connection memory: io.ReadAll over an io.LimitReader grows the destination incrementally, so a stalled client pins only bytes actually delivered (plus doubling slack). The 16 MiB cap is the mitigation working; the pinned resource is the goroutine + fd.

Recommendation noise: `MaxHeaderBytes: 1<<20` is a no-op — net/http applies DefaultMaxHeaderBytes (1<<20) when the field is 0, so inbound header size is already bounded. The fields that genuinely matter are ReadHeaderTimeout, ReadTimeout and IdleTimeout (and WriteDeadline for SSE).

mitigations_checked is accurate but incomplete: gateway.go:59 `IdleConnTimeout: 90 * time.Second` is the outbound transport to providers and does nothing for inbound sockets; and the shipped topology provides no front proxy, so no edge timeout substitutes for the missing ones (docker-compose.yml:10 publishes "${PORT:-8080}:8080", Dockerfile:27 EXPOSE 8080, repo-wide grep for nginx / client_body_timeout / proxy_read_timeout across *.md → 0 hits).
mitigations_checked: gin.Recovery (main.go:95) — panic containment only, cannot reap stalled conns. srv.Shutdown + 5s ctx (main.go:157-161) — graceful-exit only, and it itself waits on handlers that never return. Listen-retry loop (main.go:130-151) — rebinds the socket but does not drain stuck conns. Upstream context (gateway.go:496, 503, 515 `req = req.WithContext(ctx)`) — bounds the provider read for non-stream responses only; writes to the client are not context-aware. 16 MiB LimitReader (gateway.go:98, :322) — caps gateway body size, not rate. gateway.go:59 IdleConnTimeout — outbound only. TRUSTED_PROXIES empty by default (config.go:74) makes c.ClientIP() the TCP peer, so per-source mitigation would be sound, but no per-IP connection cap or accept-time limit exists anywhere in backend/. General.MaxConnections is checked only inside the gateway AuthMiddleware (gateway.go:195) — never on /api/admin/v1, /healthz, /metrics or the SPA, and never at accept time. No front proxy ships in the repo and none is documented (grep `nginx|反向代理|client_body_timeout|proxy_read_timeout|ulimit|LimitNOFILE` across *.md → 0 hits). Checked and confirmed absent: MaxBytesReader (0 hits repo-wide), http.TimeoutHandler (0 hits), net.Listener wrapper (0 hits), SetReadDeadline/SetWriteDeadline outside admin/auditws_test.go.
recommendation: On main.go:126 apply the values the config already computes plus the ones it omits: `ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second, ReadTimeout: cfg.ReadTimeout /* 90s, config.go:72 */, IdleTimeout: 120 * time.Second` (leave WriteTimeout at 0 for SSE). Then replace the unwritten half of the design: (1) on the stream path, set a per-write deadline with `rc := http.NewResponseController(c.Writer); rc.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(30*time.Second))` refreshed on each sse.go flush, and add an absolute + idle ceiling to the forwardStream loop (gateway.go:654) so a silent client cannot pin a handler; (2) bound the upstream read for streams too (scanner read deadline / per-chunk idle timer); (3) wrap inbound body reads in a deadline (e.g. 30s per read) and put http.MaxBytesReader on the admin routes, /auth/login included; (4) move the connection reservation to accept/middleware time — before auth and before the body read — and add a per-source-IP connection cap, so the overload guard covers the phases where pile-ups actually happen; (5) delete or wire cfg.WriteTimeout, and note in config.go that ReadTimeout was previously unused, since a dead knob invites the false assurance visible in gateway.go:494's comment.
reason: See the paired verify record (docs/security/raw/verify-dos-4.json) — verdict CONFIRMED, severity unchanged at high. Summary of why it is not refuted: (i) every quote lands on the cited line; (ii) the dead-config claim is reproducible by grep (`cfg.ReadTimeout`/`cfg.WriteTimeout` → 0 reads), so this is an unwired control, not a design choice; (iii) the chain has no mitigation anywhere — one http.Server, one ListenAndServe, no deadlines, no TimeoutHandler, no custom listener, no accept-time cap, no per-IP limit, no front proxy in the shipped topology; (iv) the one app-level bound that does exist (MaxConnections) is structurally unable to cover the header phase because it is enforced after header parsing and counted only inside the handler; (v) severity stays high rather than critical under this engagement's taxonomy (availability only, no RCE/authz-bypass/exfil) and stays above medium because the attack is unauthenticated, credential-free, unlogged, uncapped, and self-sustaining through the container restart policy, while the write-side half lets one API key pin all 1000 slots. The three overreaches concern only the body-phase variant's auth prerequisite, accounting and memory cost; correcting them leaves both the unauthenticated slowloris chain and the authenticated handler-pinning chain fully intact, and even surfaces a stronger unauthenticated body-read path on /auth/login.

verdict_on: dos-4 (new consequence surfaced by the same missing control)
title: Because no inbound read deadline exists, the only unauthenticated POST bodies in the product are read unbounded: /auth/login (and every other admin route) calls ShouldBindJSON with neither a size cap nor MaxConnections accounting, so a trickle body pins handlers on the management plane with no 503 back-pressure
category: unauthenticated-denial-of-service (slow-body handler + memory pile-up, management plane)
evidence: routes.go:42 `api.POST("/auth/login", s.login)` is the only functional route in the admin group without `s.AuthMiddleware()` (every sibling from routes.go:43 on carries it), and routes.go:18/21 add unauthenticated GET /healthz and GET /metrics. auth.go:29 `if err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {` decodes `struct{ Username, Password, TotpCode, RecoveryCode, MFAToken string }` (auth.go:22-28) straight from c.Request.Body. Repo-wide grep for `MaxBytesReader` returns 0 hits and for inbound `LimitReader` only gateway/gateway.go:98 and :322 — so no admin route caps its request body, and (per verify-dos-4-1) nothing sets a read deadline, so the decode blocks as long as the client dribbles bytes and its buffer grows with whatever bytes arrive. MaxConnections is never consulted on this path: the only check is gateway.go:195, inside the gateway's AuthMiddleware.
impact: This is the fully-unauthenticated slow-body primitive the filed finding wanted, on a route it did not cite. An attacker with no credentials opens N sockets to /api/admin/v1/auth/login, declares a huge body, and sends a few bytes per minute: each request occupies a handler goroutine, a conn goroutine and a readLoop goroutine, plus attacker-controlled heap for whatever JSON it manages to send (a single `"username":"AAAA..."` string is materialised verbatim), with no size ceiling and no counter that could ever return 503 — the opposite of the gateway path, which at least has a 16 MiB cap and a Conns guard. Because this is the same process that serves /v1, the memory and scheduler pressure from an unauthenticated pile-up on the management plane degrades routed LLM traffic too, and the request never reaches the bcrypt/DB stage, so no failed-login audit row, no lockout and no log line is produced: silent by construction. It also removes the 'requires a valid API key' objection that applies to the gateway body-read variant.
mitigations_checked: No limiter on this route (the quota.RateLimiter/RedisLimiter is API-key scoped: quota/quota.go:33-36 `Allow(snap *runtime.Snapshot, apiKeyID uint, alias string)`), so it cannot cover a pre-auth login; account lockout (auth.go:114-121) never fires because the handler is stuck in the body read before any credential is examined; access log (main.go:106-118) fires only after c.Next(); SQLite SetMaxOpenConns(1) serialises writes but is not reached; bcrypt cost is irrelevant pre-body. ReadTimeout on the config object (config.go:72) was clearly intended to bound exactly this and does not.
recommendation: Set `cfg.ReadTimeout` on the server (fixes the class in one line: a stalled body then dies at 90s) and add a tighter per-read deadline for bodies; wrap every admin inbound body in `http.MaxBytesReader(c.Writer, c.Request.Body, 64<<10)` (login payloads need kilobytes, not megabytes) returning 413; add an accept-phase or middleware-phase connection accounting so both planes share a bound; add a per-IP concurrent-connection cap for /api/admin/v1.

title: Sub-claims not supported as filed: MaxHeaderBytes is already bounded by net/http's 1 MiB default (so that half of the recommendation is a no-op), the gateway body-trickle variant is authenticated and counted, and no 16 MiB buffer is pre-allocated per stalled socket
evidence: main.go:126 omits MaxHeaderBytes, but Go's http.Server documents that when MaxHeaderBytes <= 0 it uses DefaultMaxHeaderBytes = 1<<20, and net/http enforces it while reading headers — so header-size blowup is already bounded and the filed 'no MaxHeaderBytes' gap costs nothing at runtime (the accompanying recommendation `MaxHeaderBytes: 1<<20` changes no behaviour). Ordering refutation for the body phase: gateway.go:195 (guard) runs in AuthMiddleware, then gateway.go:300 `s.mx.ConnInc()`, then gateway.go:322 reads the body — so a body-phase stall IS reflected in Conns() and the default General.MaxConnections = 1000 (settings/settings.go:32) will 503 further traffic at 1000; and gateway.go:322 / :98 use `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(...))`, which appends into a growing buffer rather than pre-allocating 16 MiB, so the 'multi-GB RSS from a few hundred sockets' arithmetic in the filed impact requires the attacker to actually transmit those bytes, at which point the 16 MiB cap is doing its job.
impact: No independent impact. Recorded so the audit trail is precise: the confirmed vulnerability is the absence of ReadHeaderTimeout/ReadTimeout/IdleTimeout and of any write deadline — not header size, not an unauthenticated gateway body read, not a fixed 16 MiB reservation. Correcting these three points strengthens rather than weakens dos-4, because it moves the unauthenticated body-read claim onto /auth/login (verify-dos-4-2) where it actually holds, and it removes a reviewer's easiest grounds for dismissal.
mitigations_checked: Confirmed present and therefore excluded from the finding: net/http DefaultMaxHeaderBytes header cap; the gateway's 16 MiB inbound body cap; the MaxConnections 503 shed for handler-phase pile-ups; c.Request.Context() propagation so a client that closes (rather than stalls) does unblock the upstream leg.
recommendation: None — keep the timeout wiring recommendation, drop the MaxHeaderBytes item (or add it only as explicit documentation of the intended 1 MiB limit), and do not cite the 16 MiB-per-socket memory figure in the exploit narrative.
